content: ML inference in crowdsourced-image pipelines is standardly served async via a job/message queue (Celery/RQ/SQS-style): the API enqueues the image and returns a job ID immediately (HTTP 202-style ack), a separate worker pool pulls jobs, runs inference, and publishes a completion event; the client polls or is notified. This decouples request latency from GPU/CPU-bound inference time, gives backpressure and retry semantics, and lets inference workers scale independently from the API tier. Chained-task patterns (preprocess -> detect -> persist) are standard for multi-step ML pipelines.
